sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
An accredited bachelor’s degree and sufficient mathematical preparation are needed; a mathematics major is
not an absolute requirement if ready for the graduate curriculum. Select the Mathematics PhD application.
Initial graduate admission does not itself confer formal PhD candidacy; qualifying requirements follow. [s1] [s6]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through the Graduate School and arrange at least three academic references. Identify the intended PhD
degree explicitly; the department distinguishes admission to the graduate program from later qualification for
the doctorate. [s1]
Adviser contact [Unresolved]
Graduate admissions contact: Calin Chindris, muasmathdgs@missouri.edu. No required advance adviser
agreement was located. [s1]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Apply through the Graduate School, upload records, enter referees, pay the fee, and use the status portal for
documents and decisions. An application remains valid for three semesters under central policy. [s4] [s5]
Cycle verification [2027 confirmed]
The mathematics page explicitly identifies January 15, 2027 for Fall 2027. [s1]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Standing rule]
Minimums: old TOEFL 80 with each section 17; new TOEFL 4.5 with each section 4; IELTS 6.5 with each section
6; PTE 59; Cambridge 180; DET 115. No TOEFL MyBest; IELTS One Skill Retake is accepted. Official TOEFL
reporting code is 6875. [s3]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
An earned degree OR at least two years of coursework in a recognized English-speaking country, including the
US, can exempt testing. Thus at least two years at UChicago provides a route even before degree conferral;
programs retain authority to require additional proof. TA language qualification is separate. [s3]
GRE General; GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Not required; no explicit prohibition on submitting scores was established. [s1]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Unresolved]
Teaching assistantships with tuition support are the main route. No exact current mathematics TA stipend was
found. Department fellowships can be up to USD 16,000/year, generally nonrenewable beyond one or two
years; whether a particular award supplements a TA must be confirmed. [s2]
Years of support; Extra funding application [Unresolved]
This particular funding term was not established by the public program/admissions material checked. Obtain
the exact rule in the funding offer or from the graduate coordinator; neither eligibility nor a guaranteed
amount/duration is inferred from silence. [s1] [s5]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
International doctoral applicants can receive departmental support. The department says applicants outside
North America receive support only for the PhD route. International teaching qualification remains a separate
requirement. [s1] [s2]
Conditions and duties [Unresolved]
The mathematics page describes language assessment for students without US K-12 education, with an old
TOEFL-speaking 28 exemption, and a possible one-semester residency requirement before teaching. Verify
current central TA rules and new TOEFL scoring before relying on this older formulation. [s2]
Other funding routes [Unresolved]
Competitive departmental fellowships up to USD 16,000/year are described; exact citizenship eligibility and
additional statements/reference questions are not published on the checked page. [s2]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD 100 for nonresident international applicants; USD 75 for US citizens/permanent residents. Pay on
submission; fees are nonrefundable and separate per application. [s4]
Fee waiver [Unresolved]
Central waiver categories include qualifying Missouri-resident Pell/service participants and US military

applicants. Other applicants may ask the program about fee sponsorship; mathematics sponsorship for
international applicants is not confirmed. [s4]

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic geometry and commutative algebra
Steven Dale Cutkosky
Singularities, valuations, local algebra and filtrations of ideals. [faculty1] [faculty1a]
Curators Distinguished Professor; new supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 · The Proj of the Rees algebra of a graded family of ideals
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Rankeya Datta
Positive-characteristic singularities, Frobenius methods and nonarchimedean affinoid algebras. [faculty3]
[faculty3a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · F-intersection flatness of dagger and Berkovich affinoid algebras
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Algebraic and complex geometry
Zhenbo Qin
Hilbert schemes, moduli of sheaves and maps, Gromov-Witten/Donaldson-Thomas invariants; equivariant
cohomology and vertex-operator connections. [faculty5] [faculty5a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Equivariant Chern character operators and Okounkov’s conjecture
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Algebraic geometry and representation theory
Dan Edidin
Equivariant and invariant-theoretic algebraic geometry; recent work also applies group invariants to
orbit/phase recovery and imaging. [faculty7] [faculty7a]
Marion Luther DeFoe Distinguished Professor; new supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 preprint · Orbit recovery for spherical functions
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.

Number theory
William Banks
Analytic number theory: zeta and Dirichlet L-functions, zero statistics, primes and exponential sums. [faculty9]
[faculty9a]
Current faculty; new PhD supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 revised preprint · Pair correlation for sums of two ordinates of zeros of the Riemann zeta function
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
Representation theory
Calin Chindris
Quiver representations, semi-invariants and geometric invariant theory, including combinatorial and
matrix-frame applications. [faculty11] [faculty11a]
Professor and graduate director; new supervision availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Counting 3-way contingency tables via quiver semi-invariants
Official publication evidence for the stated research match.
